bottom_line: In high-risk patients after acute coronary syndrome on antiplatelet therapy, apixaban vs placebo did not reduce cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke (hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.95; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.80 to 1.11).
implications: These data support that, in this trial, adding apixaban to antiplatelet therapy did not show a statistically significant reduction in the primary ischemic composite (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11; P = 0.51) but did increase major bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46; P = 0.001), including more intracranial bleeding (12 vs. 3) and fatal bleeding (5 vs. 0).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs placebo added to standard antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote:
We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial comparing apixaban, at a dose of 5 mg twice daily, with placebo, in addition to standard anti-
platelet therapy

major_points.text: Trial was terminated prematurely due to increased major bleeding with apixaban and no counterbalancing reduction in recurrent ischemic events.
major_points.quote:
The trial was terminated prematurely after recruitment of 7392 patients because of an increase in major bleeding events with apixaban in the absence of a counterbalanc-
ing reduction in recurrent ischemic events.

major_points.text: Intracranial and fatal bleeding events were more frequent with apixaban.

criticisms.text: Uncertainty remained regarding the effect of apixaban on ischemic events due to early stopping and fewer ischemic events than planned.
criticisms.quote:
Because this trial was stopped early owing to the
increase in bleeding events, with fewer ischemic
events having occurred than the number planned,
uncertainty remains regarding the effect of apixa-
ban on ischemic events.
